item.eigenworks.engineers_handbook.summa: In-game quick start and context-sensitive device reference.
item.eigenworks.engineers_handbook.contr: Use in air: quick start | Use on a device: its controls

tooltip.eigenworks.handbook_hint: Use the Engineer's Handbook on the placed device for full help.
message.eigenworks.welcome: EigenWorks: open Tools & Digital and use the Engineer's Handbook for an in-game quick start.
guide.eigenworks.quick_start_header: EigenWorks Quick Start — Clock to Counter
guide.eigenworks.quick_start.1: 1. In Creative, open EigenWorks: Tools & Digital.
guide.eigenworks.quick_start.2: 2. Take a Digital Clock, 8-bit Counter, Linking Tool, and Inspector.
guide.eigenworks.quick_start.3: 3. Place the clock and counter near each other; distance is not important.
guide.eigenworks.quick_start.4: 4. With the Linking Tool, use the clock first to select output 'output' (1 bit).
guide.eigenworks.quick_start.5: 5. Use the Linking Tool on the counter to connect its compatible 'clock' input.
guide.eigenworks.quick_start.6: 6. Empty-hand use the clock to enable it; the counter advances on rising edges.
guide.eigenworks.quick_start.7: 7. Use the Inspector on either block for live state and connection diagnostics.
guide.eigenworks.quick_start.8: Next: use this Handbook on any placed EigenWorks device for exact controls and ports.
guide.eigenworks.no_entry: No EigenWorks handbook entry exists for that block.
Runs a small real digital-logic/scheduler diagnostic.
Purpose: confirms the scheduler, AND gate, and rising-edge counter are operating.
Empty-hand use queues the test on the authoritative server's next engineering tick.
The chat result should report 0xC AND 0xA = 0x08 and counter = 1.
block.eigenworks.digital_clock.summary: Deterministic one-bit clock source for digital circuits.
guide.eigenworks.digital_clock.1: Output port: output (1 bit). Frequencies: 1, 2, 5, 10, or 20 Hz.
guide.eigenworks.digital_clock.2: Empty-hand use enables/disables it; sneak-use selects the next frequency.
guide.eigenworks.digital_clock.3: Use the Linking Tool on this block, then on a compatible one-bit input.
guide.eigenworks.digital_counter.1: Input: clock (1 bit). Output: output (8 bits).
guide.eigenworks.digital_counter.2: Each rising edge increments the stored value; 255 wraps to 0.
guide.eigenworks.digital_counter.3: Link a Digital Clock to clock, then inspect the live count with the Inspector.
block.eigenworks.digital_gate.controls: Use: toggle manual A | Sneak-use: change operation
guide.eigenworks.digital_gate.1: Inputs A/B and output are eight-bit digital words; NOT uses input A.
guide.eigenworks.digital_gate.2: Empty-hand use toggles manual A; sneak-use cycles the gate operation.
guide.eigenworks.digital_gate.3: Use the Linking Tool to connect compatible eight-bit output sources to its inputs.
block.eigenworks.digital_register.summar: Eight-bit storage register capturing data on a clock edge.
guide.eigenworks.digital_register.1: Inputs: data (8 bits), clock (1 bit). Output: output (8 bits).
guide.eigenworks.digital_register.2: A rising clock edge captures data; sneak-use clears the stored word.
guide.eigenworks.digital_register.3: Use the Linking Tool separately for the data source and clock source.
block.eigenworks.computer.summary: Programmable Eigen-8 CPU with RAM and debugger.
block.eigenworks.computer.controls: Use: debugger | Use with Book and Quill: assemble program
guide.eigenworks.computer.1: Write Eigen-8 assembly in a Book and Quill, then use the book on the Computer.
guide.eigenworks.computer.2: Empty-hand use opens Run, Pause, Reset, Step, registers, flags, and memory[0x0020].
guide.eigenworks.computer.3: First program: LOAD R0,25; LOAD R1,17; ADD R2,R0,R1; STORE [0x0020],R2; HALT.
block.eigenworks.microcontroller.summary: Eigen-8 MCU with GPIO, ADC, PWM, timer, UART, I2C, and SPI.
block.eigenworks.microcontroller.control: Use: run/pause | Sneak-use: reset | Book: program
guide.eigenworks.microcontroller.1: Program it by using an assembly Book and Quill on the placed MCU.
guide.eigenworks.microcontroller.2: Digital ports: gpio_in (8), gpio_out (8), pwm0 (1), and pwm_duty (8).
guide.eigenworks.microcontroller.3: Empty-hand use runs/pauses; sneak-use resets CPU and peripherals.
block.eigenworks.oscilloscope.summary: Four-channel sampled time-domain display and CSV logger.
block.eigenworks.oscilloscope.controls: Use: open scope | Sneak-use: export CSV
guide.eigenworks.oscilloscope.1: Inputs ch1–ch4 accept linked eight-bit digital sources and sample every 10 ms.
guide.eigenworks.oscilloscope.2: Empty-hand use opens traces, values, scales, channel enables, and pause.
guide.eigenworks.oscilloscope.3: Sneak-use exports bounded history beneath the server's eigenworks/exports folder.
block.eigenworks.motor_rig.summary: H-bridge, DC motor, gearbox, encoder, and protected position PID.
block.eigenworks.motor_rig.controls: Use: PID screen | Sneak-use: reset plant
guide.eigenworks.motor_rig.1: Input pwm_command is centered eight-bit PWM: 128 = zero, above/below reverses direction.
guide.eigenworks.motor_rig.2: Empty-hand use opens mode, target, Kp/Ki/Kd, and live telemetry controls.
guide.eigenworks.motor_rig.3: Outputs include setpoint, position, error, control, and encoder signals for the scope/MCU.
block.eigenworks.mathematics_workstation: Safe scalar, vector, matrix, solve, and numerical calculator.
Use: 2x2 editor | Use with Book: evaluate commands
guide.eigenworks.mathematics_workstation: Write an expression/command in a Book and Quill and use it on the workstation.
Examples include sin(pi/2), determinant, inverse, solve, integrate, and differentiate commands.
Empty-hand use opens the bounded 2x2 determinant/inverse matrix editor.
block.eigenworks.communication_hub.summa: Timed UART, I2C, and SPI transaction demonstrator.
block.eigenworks.communication_hub.contr: Use: run selected protocol | Sneak-use: change protocol
guide.eigenworks.communication_hub.1: Sneak-use cycles UART, I2C, and SPI; empty-hand use starts the selected transaction.
guide.eigenworks.communication_hub.2: Transactions use baud/clock-derived completion time rather than instant messages.
guide.eigenworks.communication_hub.3: Use the Inspector afterward to read selected protocol, status, address, and data.
block.eigenworks.robot_arm.summary: Two-link planar arm with FK, analytic IK, Jacobian, and trajectories.
block.eigenworks.robot_arm.controls: Use: next Cartesian preset | Sneak-use: reset
guide.eigenworks.robot_arm.1: Empty-hand use selects and moves toward the next reachable Cartesian target preset.
guide.eigenworks.robot_arm.2: Sneak-use resets both joint states and trajectory state.
guide.eigenworks.robot_arm.3: Inspector diagnostics show q1/q2, target, end-effector position, and manipulability.
block.eigenworks.factory_cell.summary: Conveyor, sensors, diverter, emergency stop, and scan-cycle PLC.
block.eigenworks.factory_cell.controls: Use: I/O screen | Sneak-use: emergency stop | Book: PLC program
guide.eigenworks.factory_cell.1: Use a Book and Quill containing Structured Text to compile/load the PLC program.
guide.eigenworks.factory_cell.2: Empty-hand use opens live I/O and workpiece controls; sneak-use toggles emergency stop.
guide.eigenworks.factory_cell.3: The included demo routes metallic items to DIVERTED and other items to STRAIGHT.
block.eigenworks.advanced_engineering_co: Advanced CAN, network, FPU, matrix, circuit, and IK diagnostics.
Use: parameter screen | Sneak-use: change module
guide.eigenworks.advanced_engineering_co: Sneak-use cycles the diagnostic module; empty-hand use opens its server-owned controls.
Modules cover CAN, impaired links, FPU, matrix acceleration, transient circuits, and 3R IK.
Use the Inspector to review the last result, work count, and success state.
block.eigenworks.can_cable.summary: Physical face-connected cable for 500 kbit/s CAN components.
block.eigenworks.can_cable.controls: Place between CAN Nodes; branching is supported
guide.eigenworks.can_cable.1: Place cables face-adjacent to CAN Nodes and other cables; branches are allowed.
guide.eigenworks.can_cable.2: Topology is cached when blocks load/change and is never rediscovered every tick.
guide.eigenworks.can_cable.3: Use the Inspector on a cable to confirm it belongs to a physical CAN component.
block.eigenworks.can_node.summary: Persistent node on a physical timed CAN network.
block.eigenworks.can_node.controls: Use: transmit frame | Sneak-use: change identifier
guide.eigenworks.can_node.1: Connect two or more nodes with face-adjacent CAN Cable segments.
guide.eigenworks.can_node.2: Empty-hand use transmits; sneak-use selects the next 11-bit identifier.
guide.eigenworks.can_node.3: Lower identifiers win arbitration; Inspector shows connectivity and TX/RX counts.
block.eigenworks.robot_joint_module.summ: One axis of a face-adjacent articulated robot chain.
block.eigenworks.robot_joint_module.cont: Use: rotate 90° | Sneak-use: select axis index
guide.eigenworks.robot_joint_module.1: Place modules face-adjacent in a chain and assign unique contiguous axis indices.
guide.eigenworks.robot_joint_module.2: Empty-hand use rotates the joint by 90 degrees; sneak-use changes its axis index.
guide.eigenworks.robot_joint_module.3: Loaded chains support one to six DH axes with FK and geometric Jacobian diagnostics.
